messages:
Raj: quick q — if we hit a severity issue and someone flips the feature flag for `live_rewrites`, what is the canonical handback flow? who re-enables and how do we make sure the audit trail is tamper-proof?
Ava: short answer: person who flipped it (or their manager if offline) should own the handback. but we need steps + "immutable" logging.
Sam: agreed. our current checklist is: notify #incidents, create a bug/ticket, flip with `flags` CLI which writes to audit service, and then call a post-fix verification run. but the "immutable" piece is soft right now.
Marta: can we add a WORM/append-only copy of the audit entries to the compliance bucket? that would satisfy legal for most cases. also require a ticket id in the flip command.
Raj: that sounds right. can we make the flip command enforce ticket id and operator email? example:```bash
redwood flags set live_rewrites false --by raj@redwood.com --ticket IN-6789 --reason "sev:high latency"
```
Sam: we can enforce flags CLI validation and server-side schema. we should also publish the change to our immutable stream (append-only Kafka topic + sink to s3 with object lock). ops-bot can ack with an entry id.
ops-bot: audit entry created: id=ae_20240327_4912, source=flags-cli, owner=Raj, ticket=IN-6789 :white_check_mark:
Ava: good. handback rules: (1) original owner must confirm issue resolved and post results, (2) run the canary at 10% for 30m, (3) if healthy, increase to 50% for 30m, (4) full enable. each step must be logged and linked to the ticket.
Raj: who can override if original owner is unavailable? manager or SRE lead?
Marta: Escalation matrix in play: primary owner -> oncall -> SRE lead -> security (if it touches auth). each escalation must be recorded with reason. also, any bypass requires written approval in the ticket.
Sam: we should add a small CLI helper to drive the canary rollout and log each stage automatically. sketch:```json
{
  "flag":"live_rewrites",
  "steps":[{"percent":10,"duration":"30m"},{"percent":50,"duration":"30m"},{"percent":100,"duration":"0m"}],
  "owner":"raj@redwood.com",
  "ticket":"IN-6789"
}
```
Raj: perfect. can we make the audit entry include pre/post traffic samples or perf deltas? would help the postmortem.
Sam: yes — the canary runner will snapshot latency p50/p95 and error-rate and attach to the audit entry. those snapshots are immutable once written.
Ava: operations checklist to add to runbook: 1) Flip with ticket+email, 2) Ops-bot ack and audit id, 3) Post initial verification (smoke tests + latency snapshot), 4) Canary rollout via helper, 5) Final enable + note in ticket, 6) 72h watch and finalize postmortem if severity>=P1.
Marta: small compliance note: make sure the S3 sink uses object lock with governance mode for 90 days. legal wants a copy of the audit with hash chain.
Raj: can someone own the implementation tasks? I can do CLI validation + require ticket, Sam can wire the canary runner to publish snapshots, Marta can set S3 object lock.
Sam: ping me for PR reviews — I’ll also add an ops-bot webhook to post the audit entry to the incident ticket automatically.
Ava: I’ll update the oncall runbook and add the handback bullets + escalation matrix.
Raj: thanks. one last Q — when we flip, do we also auto-create a stub postmortem template in the ticket?
Marta: yes, ops-bot can create a template with audit id, timestamps, owner, initial metrics. please include a checklist item for "was this a flag issue vs underlying service".
ops-bot: postmortem template created in IN-6789 with audit=ae_20240327_4912 :page_facing_up:
Ava: sounds good. I'll spin a small RFC doc with the checklist and link to the PRs.
Raj: awesome. thanks everyone. tagging follow-ups: @Sam for canary runner, @Marta for S3 lock, @Ava for runbook update.
Sam: noted. will start a draft PR today.
Marta: will provision the lock and share perms.
Ava: will update the runbook and ping for review.
Raj: closing this thread — will report back here when PRs are landed.
